name: Google Drive for desktop

knownPaths.description: DriveFS root. Holds one folder per signed-in account; each account folder contains the local sync database and content_cache. Deleting the account folders forces a full re-sync and can lose anything not yet uploaded. Inspect before touching.
knownPaths.inventoryDescription: Per-account folders named as long numeric IDs. Inside each is content_cache (downloaded copies of cloud files, safe to clear) next to the sync database. The same numeric IDs also appear under canceled_uploads and lost_and_found.

knownPaths.description: Local copies of files Drive downloaded from the cloud. Regenerates on demand.
Chromium Embedded Framework cache used by Drive's interface. Regenerates.

Contents of uploads Drive began and then cancelled, kept so a retry can resume instead of starting over. This is the folder that balloons during flaky uploads: a failed multi-GB upload can leave a full-size copy here. Nothing in it is part of your Drive mirror.
Older canceled-upload content moved aside during a Drive upgrade. Superseded staging data.

Where Drive banks a full copy of a local file when an upload fails and the change is rolled back. NOT disposable: if the original was since deleted or moved, this can be the only remaining copy. Check contents before removing.
DriveFS diagnostic logs. Useful when diagnosing upload failures, since the log records the failure status and whether the client timed out.
Crash reports waiting to be sent to Google.

description: Google Drive for desktop — mirrors or streams Drive content through a local DriveFS cache.
